- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and should reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates and should adjust upward, particularly if true outcome shows strong rebound.  
- Model frequently overcorrects after recent highs — if forecast rises sharply after a peak, reduce the slope of the next few points.  
- When true outcome drops sharply after a forecast peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust downward with a lagged correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply a small upward bias to initial forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model may misread trend direction — use sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid overfitting to recent extremes.
